content.title: Michigan hockey OT vs Denver Frozen Four recap: DU 4, U-M 3 (2OT)
content.text: April 9, 2026Updated April 10, 2026, 12:53 a.m. ETLAS VEGAS – Michigan hockey came to the Frozen Four with title hopes, but once again goes home empty-handed.The 1-seed Wolverines (32-7-2) lost 4-3 in double overtime to the 2-seed Denver Pioneers (27-11-3) in the national semifinal of the 2026 NCAA Hockey Tournament on Thursday, April 9, at T-Mobile Arena. The game-winning goal in the second overtime period came from Denver senior Kent Anderson, with the sudden-death goal sending the Wolverines home.Denver will take on Wisconsin, who beat North Dakota 2-1 in the other national semifinal matchup on Thursday, in the national title game on Saturday, April 11.Watch Michigan in the Frozen Four on FuboThe top overall seed Wolverines were looking for their first national championship since 1998 and their 10th overall championship, which would have tied them with Denver for the most in college hockey. Instead, the Pioneers will be playing for their 11th on Saturday.Here's how it all went down. Denver scores, advances to national championship game vs WisconsinFINAL: Denver 4, Michigan 3 (2OT).Michigan's national title hopes are over.Denver's Kent Anderson scored the game-winning goal in the second overtime period, giving the Pioneers the win pending review. Still tied in 2nd OT2nd OT, 8:41: Michigan 3, Denver 3.We have played over 90 minutes of hockey, and the score is still knotted up at 3-3.Michigan forward Jayden Perron had a shot on goal 20 seconds into the second overtime period, while Malcolm Spence had a shot on goal that actually dribbled past Denver goalie Johnny Hicks momentarily, only for Hicks to recover and cover the puck.Michigan has 21 total shots in the overtime periods to Denver's seven. Michigan vs Denver going to 2nd OTEnd OT: Michigan 3, Denver 3.Happy Friday to all of you following in Michigan (though it is still Thursday here in Las Vegas).Michigan had a one-man advantage for the last 25 seconds of the overtime period but couldn't find a scoring opportunity. They will be on the power play for the first 29 seconds of the second overtime period, which will begin at 12:25 p.m. ET.We will start with 5-on-5 hockey for another 20-minute period. Next goal wins. Denver penalty forces 4x4 hockeyOT, 1:31: Michigan 3, Denver 3.A tripping penalty on Denver forward Sam Harris gives us 4-on-4 hockey for the next minute. Denver on the power playOT, 2:26: Michigan 3, Denver 3.A slashing penalty on Michigan forward Will Horcoff gives Denver a power play with just over two minutes left in the overtime period. It is Denver's fifth power play of the game, with the Pioneers going scoreless on the previous four. Denver takes timeoutOT, 4:22: Michigan 3, Denver 3.We've had a few close calls so far, but no score in the overtime period. Michigan took its timeout in the first minute of the period and Denver now takes its timeout.If neither team scores in the overtime period, we will have an intermission followed by another 20-minute, sudden-death period. No score so far in overtimeOT, 9:35: Michigan 3, Denver 3.It's been a very physical affair so far in the overtime period, with hits and would-be penalties flying from both sides.As they have done all game, the Wolverines lead on shots 5-to-2. Michigan forward Garrett Schifsky missed a point-blank shot in front of the net off a rebound, while Asher Barnett missed another quality opportunity later in the period on a long distance slapshot.Next goal wins. Overtime period startingIt's a golden goal situation, with the next score advancing the scoring team to the national championship game against Wisconsin. Frozen Four overtime rulesTime for an overtime rules reminder!During the NCAA tournament, overtime is comprised of a 20-minute period of 5-on-5 hockey until one team scores. If no team scores after the 20-minute period, the ice is re-surfaced and the teams play another 20-minute period.There will be no 3-on-3 hockey nor will there be a shootout. Just sudden-death, 5-on-5 hockey. Michigan and Denver going to overtimeEnd regulation: Michigan 3, Denver 3.A goal from Denver freshman Clarke Caswell with under three minutes left to play sends up to overtime. Next goal wins and advances to the national championship game against Wisconsin. Denver ties game with under three minutes to play3P, 2:46: Michigan 3, Denver 3.A goal right in front of the net by Denver freshman Clarke Caswell ties the game at 3-3. Michigan 3.5 minutes from a Frozen Four win3P, 3:21: Michigan 3, Denver 2.Denver will likely press as Michigan has a 3-2 lead with just over three minutes left to go in the game. It might not be long before we see the Pioneers pull goalie Johnny Hicks for the man advantage. Jayden Perron scores, Michigan up 3-23P, 8:58: Michigan 3, Denver 2.Michigan has only had one power play so far this game, but it has made the most of it.Michigan junior Jayden Perron took a long-distance shot from the point during the man-advantage and scored the go-ahead goal for the Wolverines. If this score holds for another eight minutes, Michigan will advance to the final against Wisconsin. Michigan gets first power play3P, 9:46: Michigan 2, Denver 2.Denver defender Eric Jamieson was called for a cross-checking penalty on Michigan defender Dakoda Rheaume-Mullen, knocking him down to the ice after a Michigan shot on goal.More than 50 minutes into regulation, Michigan gets its first power play. Michigan kills another penalty3P, 12:54: Michigan 2, Denver 2.Michigan's penalty kill unit has been aces so far, killing another power play opportunity from the Pioneers.Denver has two goals, but neither have come on any of their four power plays. Denver on fourth power play3P, 14:56: Michigan 2, Denver 2.Denver got another power play, but it wasn't Tyler Duke taking the penalty.This time, it was Michigan's Garrett Schifsky, who was called for boarding. Denver will get its fourth power play when we return from the break. Denver goalie Johnny Hicks takes big hit, stays in game3P, 16:07: Michigan 2, Denver 2.Denver goalie Johnny Hicks took a big hit on a Michigan attack, dislodging the net and staying down for a couple of minutes while a Pioneers trainer attended to him on the ice.After a couple of minutes with the trainer, the referees re-attached the goal and Hicks put his helmet back on, staying in the game. Denver doesn't score on third power play3P, 17:36: Michigan 2, Denver 2.So far, there have been three penalties this game, and they've all come from Michigan defender Tyler Duke.His tripping penalty 24 seconds into the third period gave Denver its third power play of the game. But Michigan's penalty kill unit did its job once again, keeping the game tied at 2-2. Michigan tied 2-2 with Denver after two periodsEnd 2P: Michigan 2, Denver 2.Michigan has the overall shot advantage at 22-to-15, but an early goal from Denver's Cale Ashcroft was the only score of the period for either side as we take a 2-2 tie into the second intermission. Michigan has shot advantage2P, 9:48: Michigan 2, Denver 2.Denver was outshooting Michigan 10-to-4 at one point in the first period, but the Wolverines have roared back, now outshooting the Pioneers 17-to-13 midway through regulation.Unsurprisingly, Michigan senior T.J. Hughes leads the Wolverines with three shots, with his first-period goal giving the Wolverines a 2-1 lead. Denver ties game on Cale Ashcroft goal2P, 17:30: Michigan 2, Denver 2.Eleven seconds after the end of the Denver power play, Denver's Cale Ashcroft found the back of the net on a long-distance shot to tie the game for the Pioneers.The score is tied 2-2 early in the second period. Michigan kills another penalty2P, 17:41: Michigan 2, Denver 1.Michigan defender Tyler Duke was called for his second penalty of the game (and the second overall penalty of the game) on a high-stick 19 seconds into the second period.Denver got three shots on goal during the power play but couldn't break through, as the Wolverines killed another penalty. Elliot Cadeau coming back to MichiganFor some non-hockey Michigan news, Michigan basketball point guard Elliot Cadeau is officially coming back to the Wovlerines next season.Though Cadeau certainly has a hockey-sounding name, right? Is T.J. Hughes related to the Hughes brothers?The short answer is no. The longer answer can be found here, but to keep it simple, T.J. is not a Hughes brother (to the Hughes brothers you may already know, at least). Michigan takes 2-1 lead into first intermissionEnd 1P: Michigan 2, Denver 1.It was all Denver for the first 15 minutes of the first period, with the Pioneers outshooting the Wolverines 10-to-4 at one point. But Michigan turned it on thanks to a Josh Eernisse goal with less than four minutes in the period, which was followed less than a minute later by a T.J. Hughes goal off a big bounce off the boards behind the net.Denver is outshooting the Wolverines 10-to-9, but Michigan has the 2-1 lead at the first break. T.J. Hughes makes it 2-1 for Michigan1P, 2:43: Michigan 2, Denver 1.It didn't take long for Michigan to take the lead.Nearly 40 seconds after Josh Eernissee scored Michigan's first goal, Michigan senior T.J. Hughes picked up a loose puck in front of the goal and shoved it in to give the Wolverines a 2-1 lead. It's Hughes' 22nd goal of the season. Michigan ties it on Josh Eernisse goal1P, 3:41: Michigan 1, Denver 1.With 3:42 left in the first period, Michigan senior Josh Eernisse scored a goal from a faceoff, assisted by Kienan Draper.We are tied at 1-1. Denver scores first, up 1-01P, 10:31: Denver 1, Michigan 0.Denver's Kyle Chyzowski scored the first goal of the game, receiving a pass from Brendan McMorrow after Kieran Cebrian intercepted a Michigan pass in Denver's offensive zone.The Pioneers have a 1-0 lead midway through the first period. Michigan kills Denver power play1P, 11:01: Michigan 0, Denver 0.A holding penalty on Michigan defender Tyler Duke marked the first power play of the game, giving Denver a one-man advantage midway through the first period. But Michigan's penalty kill unit kept the game scoreless through the power play, and we are still level at 0-0. No score early on1P, 14:20: Michigan 0, Denver 0.Denver has been aggressive early on, outshooting the Wolverines 7-to-3 in the first five minutes of the game. But Michigan goalie Jack Ivankovic has been game, making difficult saves look easy.No score early on. Puck has droppedWe are underway here in Las Vegas, with Michigan in maize and Denver in red. Michigan takes the ice for warmupsMichigan hockey comes out with its maize jerseys ahead of its Frozen Four matchup. Michigan vs Denver delayed 15 minutesThe Michigan-Denver game, originally scheduled for 8:30 p.m. ET, will now start at approximately 8:45 p.m. according to the countdown clock at T-Mobile Arena. Wisconsin beats North Dakota 2-1, advances to Frozen Four finalNorth Dakota scored a goal with 51 seconds left in the game to bring the score to 2-1, but couldn't get the game-tying goal in the final minute as Wisconsin gets the win.Wisconsin advances to the final, looking for its first national championship since 2006. The Badgers will play the winner of the Michigan-Denver matchup, with puck drop at approximately 5:33 p.m. ET. Michigan projected lineupMichigan released its projected lines ahead of its national semifinal game against Denver, with no real surprises in the mix. Denver projected lineupDenver released its projected lines ahead of its national semifinal game against Michigan. Michigan uniforms vs DenverAs the home side for today's national semifinal matchup against Denver, Michigan will be wearing its maize uniforms. Wisconsin up after two periodsNo goals in the second period, and Wisconsin maintains a 2-0 lead after two. The Badgers are 20 minutes away from advancing to the final. Wisconsin up 2-0 in the second periodAt this rate, we're sure to get at least one Big Ten team in the Frozen Four final.Wisconsin senior winger Simon Tassy opened the scoring with a goal midway through the first period, and sophomore winger Ryan Botterill followed with a goal of his own 27 seconds later. The Badgers are up 2-0 midway through the second period. Michigan arrives to T-Mobile ArenaMichigan hockey arrived to T-Mobile Arena and greeted fans at the Frozen Four Fanfest ahead of its national semifinal matchup against Denver. Red Berenson pregame speechFormer longtime Michigan hockey coach Red Berenson spoke pregame at the Frozen Four Fest outside of T-Mobile Arena, providing words of encouragement for the Wolverines ahead of their national semifinal matchup against Denver.Berenson coached the Wolverines from 1984-2017 and led them to their last national championship in 1998. North Dakota vs Wisconsin startingThe first semifinal matchup between North Dakota and Wisconsin has started.T-Mobile Arena is about 85% full, and while there are flecks of maize in the audience, this crowd is North Dakota heavy.What time is Michigan hockey vs Denver in the Frozen FourDate: Thursday, April 9.Time: Approximately 8:30 p.m. (one hour after the conclusion of the North Dakota-Wisconsin game).Location: T-Mobile Arena, Las Vegas.What channel is Michigan hockey vs Denver in the Frozen FourPuck drop: Approximately 8:30 p.m. ET.Channel: ESPN2.Streaming: ESPN Unlimited, Fubo.Thursday's Frozen Four matchup between Michigan and Denver will be televised on ESPN2 with streaming available on Fubo.Watch Michigan vs Denver in Frozen FourMichigan hockey vs Denver predictionGoal-scoring opportunities may be scarce in this game against Denver’s defensive pressure, but when they come, Michigan will have a skater that can bury the puck in the net. Credit that to Michigan’s depth, even if the Pioneers find a way to stifle the Wolverines’ top scorers. As long as Michigan goalie Jack Ivankovic stays steady, Michigan should pull this out, even if Denver keeps it closer than Michigan fans would like.
